findings.title: New post(url, body) is not used by ConfigService.set, which still sends a GET to the removed /server/config/set/<section>/<option>/<value> route
findings.problem: This diff adds an optional JSON body to RestService.post so config-set can move to POST. Nothing calls it with a body. The backend has already moved: src/python/web/handler/config.py:25-28 registers only add_post_handler("/server/config/set", ...), and the integration test at test_config.py:226-231 confirms a GET to that path is rejected. On the frontend, src/angular/src/app/services/settings/config.service.ts:20-22 still builds /server/config/set/${section}/${option}/${value}, and line 68 still calls this._restService.sendRequest(url) (a GET). At this commit, every settings save from the UI goes to a route that no longer exists and fails, and the stored config value is never updated. The one fact I am assuming is that no later wave in this phase is meant to land in the same release; the commit history ('after wave 1') suggests a follow-up is planned, but that is not evidence the gap is harmless. pending: confirm the ConfigService.set migration to post(CONFIG_SET_URL, {section, option, value}) ships together with the backend change.
